docs.title: Brain MRI segmentation
docs.text:
A fine-tuned SegFormer-B2 for FLAIR-abnormality masks on 2D LGG MRI slices. The project provides native weights, training and serving code, and a replay with identified source data and explicit foreground measures.

Run the model · Model & weights · Source

docs.title: Current artifact and evaluation
docs.text:
Replayed on the reconstructed original patient split · 387 slices / 11 patients

Metric Value Foreground Dice 88.08% Foreground IoU 78.70%

Foreground scores pool confusion counts across all test pixels. Historical checkpoint training membership is unverified; this is not an independently established held-out benchmark or a replay of the missing U-Net baseline. Patient-macro Dice: see the full report.

Evaluation record · Pinned model

docs.title: What changed in evaluation
docs.text:
The original Kaggle cohort reproduces the expected 3133/409/387 slices and 88/11/11 patients. Preparation records file identities and rejects stale destinations. Validation and evaluation share foreground confusion-count metrics; the report includes per-patient results, bootstrap intervals and compressed prediction/target masks.

The native processor is corrected to 256², rescaling 1/255 and no ImageNet normalization. Tests compare production preprocessing, native tensors and actual model predictions.

Evaluation contract · Reproducibility · Legacy records

docs.title: Scope and reuse
docs.text:
The original U-Net baseline checkpoint is missing. The published main checkpoint's historical training membership is unverified. These limits prevent an independently established held-out benchmark or a historical architecture comparison. The limited LGG cohort and 2D input do not establish clinical validity.

Limitations · Component licenses · Training · Serving

docs.title: Evaluation records
docs.text:
The corrected replay is recorded in replay-segformer-2026-10-15.json. Its result block is generated from the artifact manifest in the README and documentation home page. It evaluates the published main weights on the reconstructed original 387-slice/11-patient split; historical training membership is unverified.

See the explicit foreground metric contract, source receipt and processor parity. The original baseline checkpoint is still absent, so a corrected historical comparison is unavailable.

docs.title: Legacy benchmark records
docs.text:
Legacy reported aggregates — metric-definition audit pending. Stored values are retained for traceability, not as verified performance claims. The Dice/IoU definitions, checkpoint/config lineage and per-patient evaluation manifest need reconciliation before comparisons.

The repository reports an evaluation size of 387 slices. The stored JSON does not include the per-slice/patient arrays or the checkpoint/config/data hashes needed to establish the complete run lineage.

Historical record Dice IoU Pixel accuracy SegFormer-B2 main 65.5% 66.2% 99.73% U-Net baseline 51.9% 57.7% 99.66%

Values remain in their original fields; they have not been swapped or recomputed. This table cannot establish a reliable architecture advantage while definitions and aggregation remain unresolved. Published plots visualize the same legacy values.

docs.title: What the audit requires
docs.text:
• Exact checkpoint and model/config hash for each report.
  • Original patient/slice evaluation manifest and mask/prediction arrays.
  • Shared foreground labels, threshold, empty-mask handling and aggregation definitions.
  • Patient-level uncertainty estimates computed from those arrays, rather than guessed confidence intervals.
  • Recorded preprocessing: the repository uses 256×256 and [0, 1]; the corrected native processor is pinned and tested against that tensor transform. The pre-fix revisions retain their original different configuration.

Reproduction commands document the workflow, without promising recovery of the old numbers. Limitations separates known source limits from unmeasured failure rates.

docs.title: Original cohort
docs.text:
The original Mateusz Buda LGG MRI dataset was retrieved on 2026-10-15, Kaggle dataset version 407317.

  • Archive: 748,584,920 bytes; SHA256 cac105de01272f0ca28dc56178f8d164a7df85d118a5b4baca388d6bcb4e854e.
  • This archive contains two identical cohort trees. Their corresponding files were compared byte-for-byte; only kaggle_3m/ was used. The clinical/genomic table is not needed for evaluation.
  • Running the preparation recipe with seed 42 recovers 3133/409/387 slices and 88/11/11 patients for train/validation/test.
  • The canonical records SHA256 is 8ea724f07ee8667c29411ce6758063c715bb6d0b6a67cd4e3cbebf38774d5391.
  • Source receipt and complete split manifest record the source, patients, image/mask filenames and SHA256 values. Dataset attribution and CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 apply to the source-derived manifest.

This reconstructs the current code's split from the original data. It does not establish historical training membership for the published checkpoint: the old run did not retain that receipt.

docs.title: Foreground overlap
docs.text:
The previous implementation passed integer B×H×W masks into torchmetrics segmentation metrics with their default one-hot input contract. Those historical aggregates remain unchanged in the legacy reports; they are not interchangeable with the corrected measures.

binary-foreground-global-v1 defines foreground as class 1 and pools integer TP, FP, FN, TN over all evaluated pixels before division:

  • Dice = 2TP / (2TP + FP + FN).
  • IoU = TP / (TP + FP + FN).
  • Pixel accuracy = (TP + TN) / (TP + FP + FN + TN); background-heavy slices can make this misleadingly high.
  • Empty prediction and target: Dice/IoU 1. Empty target with false positives: 0. No smoothing constant is added.
  • Logits are upsampled to 256² using bilinear interpolation with align_corners=False, then argmax selects the class. Masks are resized with nearest-neighbor interpolation.
  • Patient-macro scores average independently pooled patient scores. A seeded patient-cluster bootstrap reports percentile 95% intervals for cohort-pooled Dice/IoU. This is conditional on these 11 patients, not an external validation interval or a paired architecture comparison.

Validation and evaluation share the same count-based implementation. Tests cover hand-computed overlap, empty masks, invalid labels, batch invariance and changed cohort files.

docs.title: Replaying the native published artifact
docs.text:
Prepare into an empty destination (.gitkeep is allowed); stale files cause an error. Repeated runs should use a fresh output directory rather than combine old and new splits.

uv run python -m brain_mri_segmentation.data.prepare \
  --raw /path/to/kaggle_3m --out data/processed
uv run python -m brain_mri_segmentation.evaluation.evaluate \
  --hf-model kiselyovd/brain-mri-segmentation \
  --revision 838da0dff1f96aa3b87d56d2099f2b86dec483bc \
  --weights-sha256 b8e0816e76ee1f849ad37b119fc42647beba5072e842db958b848b0673dedfa4 \
  --data data/processed --out reports/replay.json

The evaluator verifies every test image and mask before inference. It writes the model identity, split hash, preprocessing and package versions, per-slice and per-patient counts, bootstrap intervals, and compressed prediction/target masks with a SHA256. The status explicitly says training_membership_verified: false for a reconstructed cohort.

For a recovered local baseline checkpoint use the same command with --checkpoint artifacts/baseline/checkpoints/best.ckpt, replacing the three HF arguments. The original U-Net checkpoint is absent from the current clone, public GitHub release and HF files. The dataset author's separately published U-Net weights are a different artifact and cannot replace this baseline in a historical replay.

docs.title: Native processor parity
docs.text:
The corrected exporter writes a 256² SegFormer processor with rescaling 1/255, no ImageNet normalization and no label reduction. The production dataset and inference CLI share data.preprocessing.image_tensor.

For an exact tensor-resize contract on input sizes other than the original 256² TIFs, pass an RGB float32 array in [0,255] to the native processor and select backend="torchvision". This avoids uint8 rounding during resizing. Focused tests compare actual pixel tensors with a maximum absolute tolerance of 3e-7, including nonsquare inputs. The published processor revision is 48c79adfde8b063e74737357ab20a6f7f67a0b1b; all other Hub files, including the weights, were unchanged. Actual model predictions matched on eight committed TIF samples and one seeded nonsquare input (zero disagreeing mask pixels); maximum tensor error was 1.79e-7 and maximum logits error was 5.25e-6. The numerical receipt records every case. This compares computation paths, not model quality. Replay intentionally pins the pre-fix revision and uses the repository transform.

See component licenses before reusing code, data or weights.

docs.title: Limitations and provenance
docs.text:
Research and education only; the repository does not provide clinical validation.

Legacy reported aggregates — metric-definition audit pending. Stored values are retained for traceability, not as verified performance claims. The Dice/IoU definitions, checkpoint/config lineage and per-patient evaluation manifest need reconciliation before comparisons.

docs.title: Known scope
docs.text:
• The source is the Buda LGG/TCGA dataset: a limited low-grade-glioma cohort, not a representative clinical population.
  • The model processes individual 2D slices, without a 3D volumetric or longitudinal context.
  • Preparation code uses a patient-level split. The stored metric files do not record the complete patient/slice manifest or checkpoint lineage of the legacy runs.
  • Input processing matters: repository inference scales RGB to [0, 1] and resizes the tensor to 256×256. The corrected native HF processor is tested against this path; use the pinned loading recipe and float32 RGB arrays described in the README.
  • The API returns a binary mask. No calibrated uncertainty or externally validated operating point is published.

docs.title: Qualitative examples
docs.text:
The published panel contains selected tumor-bearing samples. make_plots.py prefers data/sample; build_sample_data.py defaults to a training source. A recorded split/patient manifest for that panel is absent, so it must not be presented as held-out test proof.

Small lesions, ambiguous boundaries, image/sequence shift and slices without tumor are relevant cases to inspect. The new replay includes per-slice/patient counts and patient-cluster bootstrap intervals conditional on the reconstructed cohort. It does not measure external population shift or establish architecture gains. The legacy aggregate reports do not provide those uncertainty estimates.

docs.title: Before interpreting quality
docs.text: Reconcile the metric definitions and export per-patient predictions/masks with their provenance. Do not infer clinical suitability or comparative architecture capacity from the current legacy table.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
The original Kaggle cohort has been recovered with a source receipt and hashed patient/slice manifest. A new native-weight replay is recorded separately from the legacy reports; see the evaluation contract and commands. This verifies the new run without establishing the historical checkpoint's training membership.

Legacy reported aggregates — metric-definition audit pending. Stored values are retained for traceability, not as verified performance claims. The Dice/IoU definitions, checkpoint/config lineage and per-patient evaluation manifest need reconciliation before comparisons.

docs.title: Random seeds
docs.text:
• seed: 42 in configs/config.yaml is threaded through seed_everything() at the start of src/brain_mri_segmentation/training/train.py.
  • Lightning's deterministic="warn" mode avoids the nll_loss2d_forward_out_cuda_template crash while still catching non-deterministic kernels elsewhere.
  • Patient-level split is deterministic: prepare.py shuffles TCGA patient dirs with random.Random(seed=42) before the 88/11/11 partition - re-running always produces the same split.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• pyproject.toml declares direct deps; uv.lock is committed and pins every transitive package version + hash.
  • .python-version = 3.13 - CI + local dev must match.
  • CUDA torch pinned via [[tool.uv.index]] pytorch-cu124 on Win/Linux.
  • CI runs the suite against Python 3.12 + 3.13 via a matrix strategy.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
• data/sample/ (8 paired image+mask TIFs) is in git - CI + smoke tests work without any external download.
  • data/raw/ and data/processed/ are DVC-tracked. DVC remote is local-only by default.
  • Kaggle source: kaggle_3m/ (Buda et al., TCGA-LGG). 110 patient subdirs with paired *.tif + *_mask.tif.

docs.title: file_sha256
docs.text:
file_sha256(path: Path) -> str

Hash a source file without retaining its payload in memory.

Source code in src/brain_mri_segmentation/data/prepare.py 
def file_sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    """Hash a source file without retaining its payload in memory."""
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        return hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()

docs.title: build_split_manifest
docs.text:
build_split_manifest(
    raw: Path, *, seed: int, val_frac: float, test_frac: float
) -> dict

Validate paired files and record the exact deterministic patient split.

Source code in src/brain_mri_segmentation/data/prepare.py 
def build_split_manifest(raw: Path, *, seed: int, val_frac: float, test_frac: float) -> dict:
    """Validate paired files and record the exact deterministic patient split."""
    if not 0 < val_frac < 1 or not 0 < test_frac < 1 or val_frac + test_frac >= 1:
        raise ValueError("Split fractions must be positive and sum to less than one")
    patients = _collect_patients(raw)
    if not patients:
        raise ValueError(f"No TCGA_* patient dirs under {raw}")
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(patients)
    n_val = max(1, round(len(patients) * val_frac))
    n_test = max(1, round(len(patients) * test_frac))
    n_train = len(patients) - n_val - n_test
    if n_train < 1:
        raise ValueError("Not enough patients for three nonempty splits")
    splits = {
        "train": patients[:n_train],
        "val": patients[n_train : n_train + n_val],
        "test": patients[n_train + n_val :],
    }
    records = []
    basenames: set[str] = set()
    for split, members in splits.items():
        for patient in sorted(members):
            files = sorted(patient.glob("*.tif"))
            images = [p for p in files if not p.stem.endswith("_mask")]
            masks = {p.name for p in files if p.stem.endswith("_mask")}
            expected = {f"{p.stem}_mask.tif" for p in images}
            if not images or masks != expected:
                raise ValueError("Patient has empty, missing or orphan image/mask pairs")
            for image in images:
                if image.name in basenames:
                    raise ValueError("Duplicate image basename across patients")
                basenames.add(image.name)
                mask = patient / f"{image.stem}_mask.tif"
                records.append(
                    {
                        "split": split,
                        "patient": patient.name,
                        "image": image.relative_to(raw).as_posix(),
                        "mask": mask.relative_to(raw).as_posix(),
                        "image_sha256": file_sha256(image),
                        "mask_sha256": file_sha256(mask),
                    }
                )
    records.sort(key=lambda r: (r["split"], r["patient"], r["image"]))
    serialized = json.dumps(records, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
    return {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "status": "reconstructed_from_original_source",
        "algorithm": "sorted patients; Python Random(seed).shuffle; train, val, test",
        "seed": seed,
        "val_fraction": val_frac,
        "test_fraction": test_frac,
        "patient_counts": {s: len(v) for s, v in splits.items()},
        "image_counts": {s: sum(r["split"] == s for r in records) for s in SPLITS},
        "records_sha256": hashlib.sha256(serialized.encode()).hexdigest(),
        "records": records,
    }

docs.title: load_model
docs.text:
load_model(checkpoint_path: str | Path)

Load a Lightning module from checkpoint, rebuilding the backbone from hparams.

Source code in src/brain_mri_segmentation/inference/predict.py 
def load_model(checkpoint_path: str | Path):
    """Load a Lightning module from checkpoint, rebuilding the backbone from hparams."""
    import torch

    from ..models import SegmentationModule, build_model

    ckpt = torch.load(str(checkpoint_path), map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    hp = ckpt.get("hyper_parameters", {})
    model_name = hp.get("model_name")
    num_classes = hp.get("num_classes")
    if model_name is None or num_classes is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "Checkpoint missing model_name/num_classes hparams - re-train after upgrade."
        )
    backbone = build_model(model_name, num_classes=num_classes, pretrained=False)
    return SegmentationModule.load_from_checkpoint(str(checkpoint_path), model=backbone)

docs.title: Model choices
docs.text:
• Main - SegFormer-B2. Hierarchical transformer encoder (nvidia/segformer-b2-finetuned-ade-512-512, ~25 M params) with a lightweight MLP decoder. Global self-attention captures long-range texture dependencies critical in MRI - tumor regions often lack sharp boundaries and require context beyond local receptive fields. Fine-tuned with the binary segmentation head replaced.
  • Baseline - U-Net (hand-rolled). Classic encoder-decoder with skip connections; 4 levels, 32→256 channels, ~1.9 M params. The dominant architecture in medical image segmentation literature. Serves as a meaningful upper bound for CNN-only methods; the main model must beat it to justify the transformer overhead.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Metric Why Dice coefficient Primary metric - measures overlap quality; penalises both false positives and false negatives equally IoU (Jaccard) Strict overlap; harder to game than Dice; standard in segmentation benchmarks Pixel accuracy Sanity check - trivially high when background dominates, so not used for model selection

Dice is used for early stopping and checkpoint selection. Pixel accuracy is logged but not reported as headline performance because the class imbalance (tumor pixels are a small fraction of each slice) makes it an unreliable indicator.

docs.title: Key conventions
docs.text:
• Patient-level split prevents data leakage - all slices from one patient stay in the same partition.
  • Images resized to 256 × 256 before the model; masks binarised at 0.5 threshold.
  • Checkpoint stores model_name in hyperparameters so inference.load_model can rebuild the backbone without caller-supplied metadata.
  • Lightning trainer seed-controlled via Hydra seed; deterministic mode on.
